bib.title: RoboCat: A Self-Improving Generalist Agent for Robotic Manipulation

read.skipped: Reference list (about chars 71389-90358) skimmed for lineage only; Tables 6-7 numeric cells and Table 16 model list skimmed.

question: Can a single multi-embodiment, goal-conditioned transformer agent learn many manipulation tasks, adapt to new tasks and robots from 100-1000 demonstrations, and improve itself by generating data with its own fine-tuned copies?
hypothesis: Scaling and diversifying robot training data yields cross-task transfer and more efficient adaptation, and self-generated data from fine-tuned agents improves the next generalist.
contributions: a large transformer sequence model solves a large set of dexterous tasks on multiple real embodiments with differing observation and action specifications
investigation of adaptation to unseen tasks from a small set of expert demonstrations versus baselines
a simple self-improvement process that incorporates skills back into the generalist
scaling and broadening training data improves training-task performance and fine-tuning efficiency

method.summary: RoboCat is a Gato-style decoder-only transformer with a frozen pretrained VQ-GAN image tokeniser, trained by behaviour cloning with visual hindsight goals on RL, teleoperated and self-generated data from 2 sim and 3 real embodiments. A generalist is fine-tuned on 100-1000 demos per new task, deployed with learned success detectors and policy pools to collect more data, and the data is added to retrain the next generalist.
method.task: multi-task, multi-embodiment visual goal-conditioned behaviour cloning for robotic manipulation

datasets.name: Sim RL expert data (Sawyer/Panda stacking, tower, pyramid)
datasets.size: e.g. 1 022 304 episodes Sawyer RGB stacking; 1 012 142 Panda RGB stacking (Table 5)
datasets.split: all variations used; some held out for RoboCat-lim

datasets.preprocessing: images cropped/resized to 128x128x3; brightness, saturation, contrast, translation augmentation; actions scaled to [-1,1]; trailing steps trimmed using LPIPS similarity

datasets.name: Human teleoperation demos (NIST-i, YCB, vegetables, shape matching, KUKA)
datasets.size: over 4000 hours from over 100 participants; fine-tuning uses 500 or 1000 successful episodes
datasets.split: fine-tune tasks unseen in generalist training
datasets.preprocessing: as above; lifting trajectories trimmed so gripper visible in goal image

datasets.name: Self-generated data
datasets.size: episode counts in Table 8 (e.g. 4052 successes cucumber)
datasets.split: from agents fine-tuned on 500 or 1000 demos
datasets.source: fine-tuned RoboCat agents run on real robots
datasets.preprocessing: hindsight relabelling; learned reward model for semantically-equivalent goals

datasets.name: VQ-GAN pretraining images
datasets.source: ImageNet, DM Control, Meta-World, sim and real robot images (RoboCat-lim and RoboCat sets differ)

models.name: RoboCat
models.architecture: decoder-only transformer (Gato-style) with frozen VQ-GAN image tokeniser
models.tokenizer: VQ-GAN, 8x8 grid of tokens per image, 64 embeddings of dimension 128 in the quantiser

models.name: RoboCat-lim
models.architecture: same, trained only on structure-building tasks with held-out tasks

models.name: NFNet-f6 (CLIP) and Swin-L (CLIP) VFM agents
models.architecture: pretrained vision model + two MLPs + linear policy head, per-task behaviour cloning with MSE

other.candidates: 59 combinations tried; non-frozen much better than frozen

models.name: Gato; BC-IMP
models.architecture: Reed et al. 2022; Lee et al. 2021

other.note: numbers quoted from prior work, visually recounted

models.name: Success detector
models.architecture: ResNet-18 backbone, binary head, 3 basket cameras averaged

training.objective: token prediction of actions plus future image tokens k=5 steps ahead (Eq 3); hindsight and semantically-equivalent goals
training.optimizer: AdamW (pretraining), beta1 0.9, beta2 0.95, eps 1e-8; fine-tuning uses Adam
training.lr: generalist: max 1e-4, min 1e-5 (RoboCat); RoboCat-lim max 5e-6, min 5e-7; 364M max 1e-4, min 1e-5; fine-tuning constant 1e-5
training.lr_schedule: linear warm-up then cosine decay by factor 10 over 2 000 000 steps
training.steps: 2 000 000 steps cosine horizon (sim weight halved after 1 000 000); fine-tuning up to 50 000 gradient steps; VFM baselines 200 000 steps
training.regularisation: stochastic depth 0.1 in pretraining; dropout 0.1 in fine-tuning; image augmentation
training.seeds: single model per setting; no multi-run variance (model card)

other.data_weighting: task variants sampled equally; successes and failures equal; hindsight goal half the time; NIST-i successful-only with 3x weight; fine-tuning on successful episodes only
other.vqgan_training: batch size 64, 1M steps, loss 0.25*discretisation + l2 reconstruction + 0.1*log_laplace
other.checkpoint_selection: evaluate every 5000 steps for 25 episodes, then 100 episodes on best

inference.samples: 100 episodes per task (25 per checkpoint during selection), one goal image per episode
inference.prompting: visual goal image of a valid end state; no language

parameters.episode_length_and_frequency: Table 14: e.g. real Panda stacking 60 s at 10 Hz (600 steps); Sawyer vegetable lifting 20 s at 20 Hz

other.policy_pool: stateless or state-based pools reuse tasks as resets; success detectors gate eligibility

metrics.name: task success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of episodes whose last state is in the valid end-state set; real tasks counted visually by humans

eval.protocol: 100 episodes with randomised initial states and goal images; one trained model per setting, no seeds or significance tests

limits: Only one iteration of self-improvement is demonstrated.
No variance across training runs; single model evaluated (model card).
Behaviour cloning only; no RL, no language conditioning; controlled lab setting with similar backgrounds.
Self-improvement relies on human demos to seed each task, a goal-image dataset, and learned reward models with about 90% accuracy; final eval counted by hand.
Insertion with shape-matching objects stays very low (6% to 13%).
Hardware and compute not stated; weights and code not released in the paper.
Not a safety evaluation: safety discussion is qualitative in Broader Impact.
